title: Amounts Already Recovered on the Lines Before the Policyholder Is Asked for Anything
content:
What has already come back on the lines outside cover of a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is set against what the policyholder is asked to send back, so that the same money is never recovered twice.

*What is set against it where entries stand taking back what the supplement paid to someone other than the policyholder on those lines?* The amounts those entries take back.

*What is set against it where no entry stands taking back what was paid to someone else, and entries stand recording money already returned by the policyholder on those lines?* The amounts those entries record.

*What is set against it where the claim record carries neither kind of entry against those lines?* Nothing is set against it.

### Points of judgement

The first question is settled first. Where the claim record carries any entry taking back money the supplement paid to someone other than the policyholder on those lines, the amounts those entries take back are what is set against the figure, and entries recording money she has already returned do not come into it.

The second question is reached only where no such entry stands. It then takes the amounts recorded by entries recording money already returned by the policyholder on those lines.

### Hypothetical records

The claim record carries entries taking back 150.00 the supplement had paid to a provider on the lines outside cover: 150.00 is set against the figure.

The claim record carries no such entry, but entries recording 60.00 already returned by the policyholder on those lines: 60.00 is set against the figure.

The claim record carries neither: nothing is set against it.
